## ℹ️ About Us

**Rock Insurance Company** is a leading provider of personal and commercial insurance solutions, serving millions of customers nationwide through our independent agents, direct channels, and specialized home insurance products.

- **Founded:** 1978
- **Headquarters:** Columbus, Ohio
- **Employees:** 12,000+
- **Total Written Premium (YTD):** $2,393.5M

### Our Mission
> _"To protect what matters most — with integrity, innovation, and heart."_

### Core Values
- 🤝 **Integrity** — We do the right thing, always
- 💡 **Innovation** — We embrace change and technology
- 🌍 **Community** — We invest in the people we serve
- 📈 **Excellence** — We hold ourselves to the highest standards

## 💼 Business Groups

### 1. Independent Agent Group
Distributes personal and commercial lines through a national network of independent agents.
- **GWP (YTD):** $1,435.0M | **Net Income:** $139.0M

### 2. Direct Group
Sells auto, renters, and personal umbrella policies directly to consumers via digital and phone channels.
- **GWP (YTD):** $507.5M | **Net Income:** $44.8M

### 3. Home Insurance Group
Specializes in homeowners, condo, and flood insurance products with deep underwriting expertise.
- **GWP (YTD):** $451.0M | **Net Income:** $46.0M

## 🏥 Benefits Details

> Comprehensive benefits for all eligible Rock Insurance employees (full-time, 30+ hours/week). Benefits are effective on the first of the month following 30 days of employment.

### Medical Plans

| Plan | Coverage Level | Employee Monthly Cost | Deductible | Out-of-Pocket Max | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PPO Standard | Employee Only | $185/month | $750 | $4,500 | Broad national network; no referral needed for specialists |
| PPO Standard | Employee + Spouse | $420/month | $1,500 | $9,000 | Same network; spouse must not have other primary coverage |
| PPO Standard | Employee + Family | $610/month | $2,000 | $13,500 | Includes all eligible dependents under age 26 |
| HDHP | Employee Only | $95/month | $1,600 | $3,200 | HSA-eligible |
| HDHP | Employee + Spouse | $230/month | $3,200 | $6,400 | HSA-eligible |
| HDHP | Employee + Family | $340/month | $3,200 | $6,400 | HSA-eligible |

### Dental Plans

| Plan | Coverage Level | Employee Monthly Cost | Annual Max | Preventive Coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dental PPO | Employee Only | $28/month | $2,000 | 100% covered (2 cleanings/year) | Orthodontia covered at 50% up to $2,000 lifetime |
| Dental PPO | Employee + Family | $72/month | $2,000 per person | 100% covered (2 cleanings/year) | Children ortho included up to age 19 |
| Dental HMO | Employee Only | $12/month | No annual max | 100% covered | Must use in-network providers; lower out-of-pocket costs |
| Dental HMO | Employee + Family | $35/month | No annual max | 100% covered | Copays apply for major services |

### Vision Plan

| Plan | Coverage Level | Employee Monthly Cost | Exam Copay | Frames Allowance | Contact Lens Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| VSP Choice | Employee + Family | $22/month | $10 copay | $200 every 24 months per person | $150 every 12 months per person |

### 401(k) Retirement Plan

| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| Employer Match | 100% match on the first 4% of salary; 50% match on the next 2% (up to 5% total company match) |
| Vesting Schedule | Immediate vesting on employee contributions; 3-year graded vesting on employer match (33%/66%/100%) |
| Eligible Investments | Target-date funds, S&P 500 index, bond funds, international equity, stable value, self-directed brokerage window |
| Auto-Enrollment | Yes — 3% default pre-tax contribution; auto-escalation of 1% annually up to 10% |
| Roth 401(k) Option | Yes — available for all participants |
| Loan Provisions | Up to 50% of vested balance or $50,000 (whichever is less); repayment within 5 years |
| Hardship Withdrawal | Available for qualifying events (medical expenses, home purchase, tuition, eviction prevention) |

## 📖 Employee Handbook

> Key policies and guidelines. This section summarizes critical handbook content. The full Employee Handbook is available for [download (PDF)](#).

### Code of Conduct

Rock Insurance expects all employees to uphold the highest standards of professional and ethical behavior. Every team member is an ambassador of our brand and values.

- **Professional behavior:** Treat colleagues, customers, agents, and partners with respect and courtesy. Collaborate openly and communicate honestly.
- **Ethical standards:** Conduct all business dealings with integrity. Never misrepresent products, coverage, or company policies. Follow all applicable laws and regulations.
- **Conflicts of interest:** Disclose any personal, financial, or family relationships that could influence business decisions. Do not accept gifts valued over $100 from vendors or clients without manager and Compliance approval.
- **Confidentiality:** Protect company proprietary information, customer data, and trade secrets. Do not share confidential information outside authorized channels. This obligation continues after separation from the company.
- **Use of company resources:** Company equipment, systems, and funds are for business purposes. Limited personal use is permitted but must not interfere with work duties or violate any policies.
- **Reporting violations:** Report suspected violations to your manager, HR, or the Compliance Hotline (compliance@rockinsurance.com). All reports are taken seriously and investigated promptly. Retaliation against good-faith reporters is strictly prohibited.

### Dress Code

| Work Setting | Dress Code | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Corporate Office | Business casual | Collared shirts, blouses, slacks, skirts, closed-toe shoes |
| Client-Facing Meetings | Business professional | Suits, blazers, ties, professional dresses, dress shoes |
| Casual Friday | Relaxed casual | Jeans (no rips), sneakers, polo shirts, company-branded apparel |
| Remote Work | Presentable on camera | Business casual from waist up for video calls; comfortable attire off-camera |
| Field / Claims Adjusters | Company-branded field attire | Rock Insurance polo, khakis or cargo pants, steel-toe boots where required, high-vis vest for site visits |

### Anti-Harassment & Non-Discrimination Policy

Rock Insurance maintains a zero-tolerance policy for harassment, discrimination, and retaliation in any form. We are committed to providing a workplace free from unlawful conduct for all employees, contractors, vendors, and visitors.

- **Protected categories:** Race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and any other category protected by federal, state, or local law.
- **What constitutes harassment:** Unwelcome verbal conduct (slurs, jokes, derogatory comments), physical conduct (unwanted touching, blocking movement), visual conduct (offensive posters, emails, gestures), and sexual harassment (unwanted advances, requests for favors, quid pro quo).
- **Reporting channels:** Employees may report to their direct manager, any member of HR, or the Compliance Hotline (compliance@rockinsurance.com). Reports may be made anonymously.
- **Investigation process:** All reports are investigated promptly and confidentially by HR and/or Compliance within 5 business days of receipt. Both parties are interviewed, evidence is reviewed, and findings are documented.
- **Retaliation protections:** Retaliation against anyone who reports, participates in an investigation, or opposes discriminatory practices is strictly prohibited and is itself grounds for discipline up to termination.
- **Required training:** All employees must complete Anti-Harassment training annually. Managers must complete an additional Manager's Responsibility module.

### Disciplinary Process

| Step | Action | Documentation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Verbal Warning | Manager documents conversation in HR system; employee acknowledges discussion |
| 2 | Written Warning | Formal written notice outlining the issue, expected improvement, and timeline; signed by employee and manager |
| 3 | Final Written Warning / PIP | Performance Improvement Plan with specific goals, 30–60 day timeline, and weekly check-ins; HR involvement required |
| 4 | Suspension | Paid or unpaid suspension (1–5 days) pending investigation or as disciplinary measure; HR and Legal notified |
| 5 | Termination | Employment separation; conducted by HR with manager present; exit interview and final pay processed per state law |

> Note: Certain offenses (e.g., fraud, violence, theft) may result in immediate termination without progressive discipline.

### Workplace Safety

Rock Insurance is committed to providing a safe and healthy workplace for all employees, in compliance with OSHA and applicable state regulations.

- **OSHA compliance:** All facilities undergo annual OSHA compliance audits. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are maintained for all applicable materials. Employees have the right to report unsafe conditions without fear of retaliation.
- **Emergency procedures:** Emergency exits are clearly marked. Evacuation maps are posted on every floor. Emergency wardens are assigned per floor — see your floor's evacuation map for meeting points.
- **Fire evacuation:** Exit the building immediately via the nearest stairwell (do NOT use elevators). Proceed to designated assembly points in the parking lot. Check in with your floor warden. Do not re-enter until the all-clear is given.
- **First aid stations:** Located on every floor near the main elevator bank. AED devices are available in each lobby and break room. CPR/First Aid trained volunteers are listed on the Safety Board.
- **Workers' compensation:** All work-related injuries must be reported to your manager and HR within 24 hours. Complete an Incident Report form (available on the HR Portal). Medical treatment is covered under the company's workers' compensation policy.
- **Incident reporting:** Report all workplace injuries, near-misses, and hazards via the Incident Report form on the HR Portal or email safety@rockinsurance.com.

### Drug-Free Workplace Policy

Rock Insurance maintains a drug-free workplace to ensure the safety, health, and productivity of all employees.

- **Prohibited substances:** The use, possession, distribution, or sale of illegal drugs, controlled substances, or unauthorized alcohol on company premises or during work hours is strictly prohibited.
- **Testing policy:** Pre-employment drug screening is required for all new hires. Random testing applies to safety-sensitive positions. Post-accident testing is conducted when workplace injuries occur. Reasonable suspicion testing may be initiated by a trained supervisor.
- **Prescription medications:** Employees taking prescription medications that may impair performance must notify HR (confidentially). Accommodations will be made where possible while ensuring workplace safety.
- **Consequences of violations:** First violation results in mandatory referral to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and possible suspension. Second violation results in termination. Refusal to submit to testing is treated as a positive result.
- **Employee Assistance Program (EAP):** Free, confidential support is available 24/7 at 1-800-555-ROCK. Services include substance abuse counseling, rehabilitation referrals, and up to 8 sessions per issue at no cost.

### Social Media Policy

Rock Insurance recognizes that employees use social media in their personal and professional lives. This policy provides guidelines to protect both employees and the company.

- **Acceptable use:** Employees may use personal social media accounts during breaks or outside work hours. Do not let social media use interfere with job responsibilities.
- **Company representation:** Only authorized Communications and Marketing team members may post on behalf of Rock Insurance. Do not create accounts that could be mistaken for official company channels.
- **Confidentiality:** Never share confidential company information, proprietary data, customer details, financial results, or internal strategies on social media.
- **Personal vs. professional accounts:** If you identify yourself as a Rock Insurance employee online, include a disclaimer: "Views are my own and do not represent Rock Insurance." Do not use your Rock Insurance email for personal social media sign-ups.
- **Consequences of violations:** Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination, depending on severity. Content that harasses, discriminates, or threatens others is grounds for immediate action.
- **Approved handles:** @RockInsurance (Twitter/X), @RockInsuranceCompany (LinkedIn, Facebook), @rock_insurance (Instagram). Brand guidelines are available on the Marketing SharePoint site.

## 🏠 Remote Work Policy

> Rock Insurance supports flexible work arrangements to attract and retain top talent while maintaining productivity and collaboration.

### Eligibility

| Criteria | Details |
|---|---|
| Eligible Roles | Roles that do not require daily on-site presence (e.g., IT, Finance, Marketing, HR, Underwriting analysis). Excludes mailroom, facilities, and field adjusters. |
| Minimum Tenure | 90 days in current role (waived for positions hired as remote) |
| Performance Requirement | "Meets Expectations" or above on most recent performance review |
| Manager Approval | Required |
| HR Approval | Required for fully remote arrangements; hybrid arrangements require manager approval only |

### Work Arrangements

| Arrangement | Description | In-Office Days | Eligibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fully On-Site | Employee works from a Rock Insurance office full-time | 5 days/week | All employees |
| Hybrid | Employee splits time between office and home on a set schedule | 2–3 days/week (set by manager) | Employees in eligible roles with 90+ days tenure and "Meets Expectations" rating |
| Fully Remote | Employee works from home or approved remote location full-time | 0 days/week | Select roles only; requires VP and HR approval; must reside in a state where Rock Insurance has a business presence |

### Equipment & Stipend

| Item | Provided By | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Laptop | Company | Dell Latitude or MacBook Pro (role-dependent); refreshed every 3 years; includes standard software image |
| Monitor | Company | One 27" external monitor provided upon request; submit IT ticket for delivery |
| Keyboard & Mouse | Company | Wireless keyboard and mouse kit included with laptop order |
| Home Office Stipend | Company | $500 one-time setup stipend for new remote/hybrid employees; receipts required within 60 days |
| Internet Reimbursement | Company | $75/month reimbursement for home internet; submitted via monthly expense report |
| Office Chair | Employee (reimbursable) | Up to $350 reimbursed for ergonomic chair purchase; must meet ergonomic guidelines (see HR Portal) |

### Expectations & Guidelines

- **Core working hours:** All remote and hybrid employees must be available 9:00 AM – 3:00 PM ET for meetings and real-time collaboration, regardless of time zone.
- **Response time expectations:** Teams chat messages — respond within 30 minutes during core hours. Email — respond within 4 business hours. Urgent escalations — respond immediately via phone or Teams call.
- **Camera-on policy:** Cameras should be on for all team meetings, 1:1s, and client/agent calls. Cameras optional for large all-hands or training webinars.
- **Workspace requirements:** Employees must have a dedicated workspace with a door or separation from household activity. Workspace must have reliable internet (minimum 25 Mbps download) and be free from excessive noise.
- **Data security:** Company data must only be accessed via company-issued devices. VPN must be active when accessing internal systems. Screens must be locked when stepping away. Confidential phone calls must be taken in a private setting.
- **Time tracking / availability:** Hybrid and remote employees must keep Outlook calendar up-to-date. Set Teams status accurately (Available, Busy, Away). Log work hours in Workday if applicable to your role.
- **In-person requirements:** All remote employees must attend quarterly team on-site days (travel expenses covered). Hybrid employees must attend their scheduled in-office days — schedule changes require 2 weeks' notice.

### Communication Norms

| Channel | Use For | Expected Response Time |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft Teams Chat | Quick questions, informal check-ins, project updates, daily standups | Within 30 minutes during core hours |
| Email | Formal communications, cross-department requests, documentation trails, external contacts | Within 4 business hours |
| Phone / Teams Call | Urgent issues, sensitive conversations, complex discussions that need real-time dialogue | Immediate for urgent; schedule for non-urgent |
| Teams Meetings | Team syncs, project reviews, client presentations, training sessions | Join on time; respond to invites within 24 hours |

| 4 | How do I access my employee file? | Submit a request via the HR Portal or email hr@rockinsurance.com. HR will schedule a time for you to review your file within 5 business days. Per company policy, reviews take place in the HR office or via secure video. |
| 5 | Who do I contact for workplace accommodations? | Contact HR at hr@rockinsurance.com or ext. 5100. The HR team will work with you through an interactive process to determine reasonable accommodations under the ADA. All requests are confidential. |

| 2 | How do I add a dependent to my insurance? | Log in to Workday → Benefits → Change Benefits → Add Dependent. You'll need the dependent's SSN and date of birth. Must be completed within 30 days of the qualifying event (birth, marriage, adoption). |

| 4 | How do I find an in-network provider? | Visit the carrier's website — Anthem (medical), Delta Dental (dental), or VSP (vision). Links are available on the Benefits page of the HR Portal. You can also call the number on the back of your insurance card. |
| 5 | How does the 401(k) match work? | Rock Insurance matches 100% of the first 4% of your salary and 50% of the next 2%, for a maximum company match of 5%. The match is deposited each pay period. Employer match follows a 3-year graded vesting schedule. |
| 6 | How do I access the Employee Assistance Program (EAP)? | Call 1-800-555-ROCK (available 24/7) or visit www.rockwellness.com. The EAP provides up to 8 free confidential counseling sessions per issue, plus referrals for legal, financial, and family services. |

## 🖥️ IT Policies & Self-Service

> Technology policies, self-service guides, and IT support resources.

### VPN Setup Guide

**Step-by-step instructions for connecting to the Rock Insurance VPN:**

1. **Download the VPN client:** Install Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client v4.10+ from the [IT Self-Service Portal](#) or request installation via IT Help Desk (ext. 5000).
2. **Open Cisco AnyConnect** and enter the VPN server address: `vpn.rockinsurance.com`
3. **Enter your credentials:** Use your network username (first.last) and password.
4. **Complete MFA:** Approve the push notification in the Microsoft Authenticator app, or enter the 6-digit code.
5. **Verify connection:** The AnyConnect icon in the system tray will show a locked padlock when connected. Test by accessing an internal site (e.g., intranet.rockinsurance.com).

**Troubleshooting:**
- *"Connection attempt failed"* — Ensure you are connected to the internet. Restart AnyConnect and try again.
- *"Authentication failed"* — Verify your password hasn't expired (check at password.rockinsurance.com). Ensure MFA is set up correctly.
- *"Unable to establish VPN"* — Disable any personal firewall or VPN software that may conflict. Restart your laptop.
- **Still having issues?** Contact IT Help Desk at ext. 5000 or helpdesk@rockinsurance.com (24/7 support).

### Password Policy

| Requirement | Details |
|---|---|
| Minimum Length | 14 characters |
| Complexity | Must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number, and one special character (!@#$%^&*) |
| Expiration | Every 90 days; notification sent 14 days and 3 days before expiration |
| History | Cannot reuse the last 12 passwords |
| Lockout | 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes = 30-minute lockout; after 3 lockouts, account requires IT Help Desk reset |
| Self-Service Reset | [Password Reset Portal](password.rockinsurance.com) — verify identity via MFA |
| MFA Required | Yes — Microsoft Authenticator app (primary), SMS to registered mobile (backup); required for VPN, email, and all internal portals |

### Software Request Process

| Step | Action | SLA |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Submit request via [IT Service Portal](#) | — |
| 2 | Manager approval | 1 business day |
| 3 | IT security review (if required) | 2 business days (only for non-approved software; pre-approved apps skip this step) |
| 4 | Installation / provisioning | 1–2 business days after approval; remote push for standard software, scheduled session for complex installs |

### BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) Policy

| Aspect | Policy |
|---|---|
| Eligible Devices | Smartphones (iOS 16+ / Android 13+), tablets; personal laptops are NOT eligible for company network access |
| Required Security | MDM enrollment (Microsoft Intune), device encryption enabled, PIN/biometric lock (6+ digit PIN), automatic OS updates enabled |
| Company Data on Personal Devices | Accessed only through managed apps (Outlook, Teams, OneDrive); no downloading of sensitive data to personal storage |
| Remote Wipe Consent | Required — IT reserves the right to remotely wipe company data (managed partition only) if device is lost, stolen, or upon employment termination |
| Reimbursement | $50/month mobile device stipend for BYOD participants who use personal phones for work purposes |

### Approved Software & Tools

| Category | Tool(s) | License Type |
|---|---|---|
| Email & Calendar | Microsoft Outlook / Office 365 | Enterprise E5 |
| Collaboration | Microsoft Teams | Enterprise E5 |
| File Storage | OneDrive (personal), SharePoint (team) | Enterprise E5 |
| Project Management | Jira (Engineering), Azure DevOps (IT), Microsoft Planner (general) | Enterprise / Team |
| Development | VS Code, GitHub Enterprise, IntelliJ IDEA | Enterprise |
| CRM | Salesforce Sales Cloud | Enterprise |
| Analytics | Power BI Pro, Tableau Desktop (select teams) | Enterprise / Named User |

### Email & Communication Standards

**Acceptable Use:**
- Company email is for business purposes. Limited personal use is allowed but must not interfere with work, consume excessive storage, or violate any policy.
- Do not use company email to register for personal social media, shopping, or non-work services.

**Email Signature Format:**
> **[Full Name]** | [Title]
> Rock Insurance | [Department]
> [Phone/Extension] | [email]
> rockinsurance.com

**Additional Standards:**
- Maximum attachment size: 25 MB (use OneDrive sharing links for larger files).
- External email warning: Emails from outside the organization display a yellow banner — "This message originated from outside Rock Insurance. Exercise caution with links and attachments."
- Teams etiquette: Use status indicators accurately, mute in large meetings, use threads in channels, avoid @everyone unless critical, respect Do Not Disturb status.

### Data Classification

| Level | Description | Examples | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Public | Information approved for external sharing with no restrictions | Press releases, published marketing materials, job postings | May be shared freely; no special handling required |
| Internal | General business information for employees only | Internal memos, org charts, meeting notes, process docs | Keep within Rock Insurance systems; do not share externally without approval |
| Confidential | Sensitive business data requiring access controls | Financial reports, strategic plans, employee records, pricing models, agent data | Encrypt in transit and at rest; share only on need-to-know basis; label documents "Confidential" |
| Restricted | Highly sensitive data subject to regulatory requirements | Customer PII/PHI, SSNs, payment card data, claims medical records, credentials | Strongest controls — encryption required, access logged, DLP policies enforced, no local storage, breach notification required if exposed |

> 📌 IT Help Desk: helpdesk@rockinsurance.com / ext. 5000 (24/7)

## 📘 Glossary of Insurance Terms

> Common insurance terms used across Rock Insurance. Helpful for new hires and non-insurance staff.

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Actual Cash Value (ACV) | The replacement cost of damaged or stolen property minus depreciation. Reflects the item's current market value at the time of loss. |
| Adjuster | A professional who investigates insurance claims, evaluates the damage or loss, and determines the amount the insurance company should pay. |
| Binder | A temporary agreement that provides insurance coverage until the formal policy is issued. Typically valid for 30–60 days. |
| Catastrophe (CAT) | A natural or man-made event that causes widespread damage and a significant number of insurance claims (e.g., hurricanes, earthquakes, wildfires). Industry-defined as an event causing $25M+ in insured losses. |
| Claim | A formal request by a policyholder to the insurance company for coverage or compensation for a covered loss or policy event. |
| Combined Ratio | A measure of insurance company profitability calculated as (Incurred Losses + Expenses) ÷ Earned Premiums. A ratio below 100% indicates underwriting profit. |
| Deductible | The amount the policyholder must pay out-of-pocket before the insurance company begins to pay on a claim. Higher deductibles typically result in lower premiums. |
| Endorsement | An amendment or addition to an existing insurance policy that modifies the terms or coverage (also called a "rider"). Examples: adding scheduled jewelry, water backup coverage. |
| Exclusion | A provision in an insurance policy that specifies risks, perils, or conditions that are NOT covered. Common exclusions include flood (on homeowners), intentional acts, and normal wear and tear. |
| FNOL (First Notice of Loss) | The initial report made to an insurance company by the policyholder (or a third party) when a loss or incident occurs. FNOL triggers the claims process. |
| Gross Written Premium (GWP) | The total premium revenue written by an insurance company before any deductions for reinsurance. A key measure of business volume. |
| Indemnity | The principle of restoring the insured to the same financial position they were in before the loss, no more and no less. Prevents the policyholder from profiting from a loss. |
| Liability | Legal responsibility for one's acts or omissions. In insurance, liability coverage pays for damages and legal defense when the policyholder is found responsible for injury or property damage to others. |
| Loss Ratio | Incurred Losses ÷ Earned Premiums. Measures the percentage of premium income used to pay claims. A lower loss ratio indicates better underwriting performance. |
| Net Combined Ratio | Combined ratio calculated after the effect of reinsurance, reflecting the company's retained underwriting profitability. |
| Net Pure Loss Ratio | Incurred losses net of reinsurance ÷ Earned premiums net of reinsurance. Isolates core loss experience without expense loading. |
| Policy | A written contract between the insurance company and the policyholder that outlines the terms, conditions, coverage, exclusions, and premium for the insurance provided. |
| Premium | The amount of money the policyholder pays (monthly, quarterly, or annually) to the insurance company in exchange for coverage. Premium is based on risk assessment, coverage limits, and deductible. |
| Reinsurance | Insurance purchased by an insurance company from another insurer to limit its exposure to large losses. Helps spread risk and stabilize financial results. |
| Replacement Cost | The cost to replace damaged or stolen property with new property of similar kind and quality, without deducting for depreciation. Provides higher payouts than ACV. |
| Rider | An optional add-on to a standard insurance policy that provides additional benefits or coverage. Similar to an endorsement. Examples: identity theft rider, equipment breakdown rider. |
| Subrogation | The process by which an insurance company, after paying a claim, seeks reimbursement from the party responsible for causing the loss. Helps recover costs and keep premiums lower. |
| Surplus Lines | Insurance coverage provided by non-admitted insurers (not licensed in the state) for risks that standard admitted carriers are unwilling to cover. Subject to separate state regulation. |
| Underwriting | The process of evaluating, selecting, and pricing insurance risks. Underwriters analyze applications, assess risk factors, and determine premium rates and coverage terms. |
| Uninsured / Underinsured Motorist | Coverage that protects the policyholder when they are injured by a driver who has no insurance (uninsured) or insufficient insurance (underinsured) to cover the damages. Required in many states. |

## 📝 Claims Handling Process

> Overview of the end-to-end claims lifecycle at Rock Insurance.

### Claims Lifecycle

```
1. FNOL (First Notice of Loss)
   ↓
2. Claim Assignment
   ↓
3. Investigation & Documentation
   ↓
4. Coverage Determination
   ↓
5. Damage Evaluation / Estimation
   ↓
6. Settlement Negotiation
   ↓
7. Payment / Resolution
   ↓
8. Claim Closure
```

### Detailed Process Steps

| Step | Description | SLA | Responsible |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. FNOL | Policyholder reports loss via phone (1-800-555-ROCK), online portal (claims.rockinsurance.com), mobile app, or through their independent agent. Basic details captured: policy number, date/time of loss, description, injuries, police report number. | Acknowledge within 24 hours; assign claim number immediately | FNOL Intake Team |
| 2. Claim Assignment | System auto-assigns claim to an adjuster based on claim type (auto, home, commercial), severity, location, and adjuster workload. Complex or high-value claims are manually triaged by the Claims Manager. | Assignment within 4 business hours of FNOL | Claims Assignment System / Claims Manager |
| 3. Investigation | Adjuster contacts policyholder within 24 hours, gathers documentation (photos, police reports, witness statements, medical records), and inspects damage (field or virtual). Third-party experts engaged as needed (engineers, medical professionals). | Initial contact within 24 hours; investigation substantially complete within 15 business days | Claims Adjuster |
| 4. Coverage Determination | Adjuster reviews the policy, verifies coverage applies, checks for exclusions or limitations, confirms deductible, and determines if the loss is covered. If coverage is denied, a detailed denial letter is issued. | Coverage decision within 5 business days of investigation completion | Claims Adjuster / Claims Manager |
| 5. Damage Evaluation | For property claims: field inspection or contractor estimates. For auto: estimate via CCC Intelligent Solutions or in-person appraisal. For injury claims: medical review and independent medical exam if warranted. | Estimate completed within 10 business days | Claims Adjuster / Vendor Partners |
| 6. Settlement | Adjuster presents settlement offer to policyholder. Negotiations may occur. For disputes, the file is escalated to Claims Manager or mediation. Supplemental claims are accepted if additional damage is discovered. | Initial offer within 5 business days of evaluation; negotiations within 30 days | Claims Adjuster / Claims Manager |
| 7. Payment | Payment issued via direct deposit (preferred), check, or two-party check (if lender involved). Partial payments may be issued for undisputed portions while disputed amounts are resolved. | Payment within 5 business days of settlement agreement | Claims Payment Team |
| 8. Closure | Adjuster completes final file review, confirms all payments made, sends closing letter to policyholder, and records outcome in claims system. Customer satisfaction survey sent automatically. | File closed within 10 business days of final payment | Claims Adjuster |

### Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Claims Adjuster | Primary point of contact for the policyholder; investigates claims, evaluates damages, determines coverage, negotiates settlements, and issues payments. Manages a caseload of 80–120 open claims. |
| Claims Manager | Supervises a team of 10–15 adjusters; reviews complex claims and escalations; approves settlements above adjuster authority ($50K+); ensures compliance with state regulations and company guidelines. |
| Special Investigations Unit (SIU) | Investigates suspected fraudulent claims; conducts surveillance, background checks, and forensic analysis; works with law enforcement; refers cases for prosecution when appropriate. Handles approximately 5% of all claims. |
| Vendor / Contractor | Preferred network of body shops, restoration companies, and contractors who perform repairs. Vendors are vetted for quality, pricing, and customer service. Managed by the Vendor Management team. |
| Legal (if litigated) | In-house and outside counsel handle claims that enter litigation. Legal works with the adjuster on defense strategy, discovery, depositions, and trial preparation. Engaged when a demand or lawsuit is filed. |

### Escalation Path

| Level | Condition | Escalated To | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Customer complaint, dissatisfaction with adjuster response, minor coverage question | Claims Manager | Response within 24 hours |
| 2 | Coverage dispute, settlement disagreement above $50K, potential bad faith concern | Claims Director | Review within 48 hours |
| 3 | Litigation filed, suspected bad faith, regulatory inquiry, claims over $500K | VP Claims / Legal | Immediate engagement; strategy meeting within 24 hours |
| 4 | State regulatory complaint, Department of Insurance inquiry, media attention | CLO / Compliance | Response within 4 business hours |

### Quality Assurance

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Claims Closure Rate | 85% of claims closed within 30 days | Monthly dashboard; reviewed in weekly Claims leadership meeting |
| Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) | 4.5 / 5.0 or higher | Post-claim survey sent at closure; results aggregated monthly by team and adjuster |
| Average Cycle Time | 18 days (auto), 25 days (home), 35 days (commercial) | Measured from FNOL to closure; tracked in claims management system |
| Reopened Claims Rate | Less than 3% of closed claims reopened within 12 months | Monthly audit; root cause analysis on all reopened claims |
| Audit Score | 95% or above on quarterly file audits | Random sample of 10% of closed files; scored on documentation, compliance, and accuracy |

## ⚖️ Compliance & Regulatory Summary

> Key compliance and regulatory requirements for Rock Insurance operations.

### Regulatory Framework

Rock Insurance operates under a complex regulatory framework that spans federal and state levels. Key components include:

- **State insurance department oversight:** Each of the 50 states (plus DC) has a Department of Insurance (DOI) that regulates rates, policy forms, market conduct, and financial solvency. Rock Insurance holds licenses and files annual statements in all operating states. The Ohio Department of Insurance is our domiciliary regulator.
- **NAIC guidelines:** Rock Insurance follows National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) model laws and guidelines, including the Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act, Market Conduct Surveillance model, and Risk-Based Capital requirements.
- **Federal regulations:** Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) — customer data privacy and information security; Dodd-Frank Act — systemic risk oversight (applicable to larger insurers); Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA) — mandatory terrorism coverage offer; Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) — use of credit in underwriting; OFAC / sanctions compliance — ensuring no transactions with sanctioned persons or entities.
- **Key state-specific requirements:** California CCPA/CPRA — consumer data privacy rights; New York Regulation 187 — best interest standard for life/annuity sales; Florida Homeowners — Citizens depopulation participation; Texas — prompt payment rules (15-day acknowledgment, 15-day acceptance/denial); All states — unfair claims settlement practices acts.

### Mandatory Training Calendar

| Training | Frequency | Due Date | Audience | Platform |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anti-Money Laundering (AML) | Annual | January 31, 2026 | All employees | [LMS Portal](#) |
| Anti-Harassment | Annual | February 28, 2026 | All employees | [LMS Portal](#) |
| Data Privacy (GLBA / CCPA) | Annual | March 15, 2026 | All employees | [LMS Portal](#) |
| Ethics & Compliance | Annual | March 31, 2026 | All employees | [LMS Portal](#) |
| Producer Licensing CE | Per state requirement (biennially in most states) | Varies by state — check license expiration in Sircon | Licensed agents and producers | State-approved CE providers (WebCE, Kaplan, The Institutes) |
| OFAC / Sanctions | Annual | June 30, 2026 | Underwriting, Claims, Finance, Compliance | [LMS Portal](#) |

### Audit Schedule

| Audit Type | Frequency | Next Scheduled | Conducted By |
|---|---|---|---|
| Internal Audit | Quarterly | Q2 2026 (April) | Internal Audit team (reports to Audit Committee of the Board) |
| State Regulatory Exam | Every 3–5 years (per NAIC cycle) | Ohio DOI exam scheduled Q3 2026 | Ohio Department of Insurance / Zone examiners |
| Financial Audit (External) | Annual | March 2026 (for FY 2025) | Deloitte & Touche LLP |
| SOX Compliance | Annual | Q4 2026 | Internal Audit with Deloitte advisory |
| Data Privacy Audit | Annual | September 2026 | IT Security + External assessor (Coalfire) |

### Reporting Requirements

| Report | Filed With | Frequency | Responsible |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual Statement | State Departments of Insurance (all operating states) via NAIC | Annual (due March 1) | CFO / Actuarial / Financial Reporting |
| Quarterly Financials | NAIC, domiciliary state | Quarterly (45 days after quarter-end) | Financial Reporting team |
| Market Conduct Reports | State DOI (as requested or per schedule) | As required; triennial in key states | Compliance / Legal |
| Complaint Logs | State DOI, NAIC Complaint Database | Quarterly | Compliance team; tracked in CMS and reported to NAIC via CDR |

### Whistleblower Protections

Rock Insurance is committed to an ethical workplace and encourages all employees to report suspected fraud, waste, abuse, or violations of law or company policy.

- **Anonymous reporting channels:** Compliance Hotline — compliance@rockinsurance.com (monitored by Compliance team, separate from management chain). Anonymous third-party hotline: 1-888-555-ROCK (operated by EthicsPoint). Online reporting form available on the Compliance Portal.
- **Non-retaliation guarantee:** Rock Insurance strictly prohibits retaliation of any kind against individuals who report concerns in good faith. Retaliation includes adverse employment actions, intimidation, threats, or discrimination. Violators of the non-retaliation policy are subject to discipline up to termination.
- **Investigation process:** All reports are reviewed by the Chief Compliance Officer within 48 hours. Investigations are conducted confidentially by the Compliance or Internal Audit team. Findings are reported to the Audit Committee. Reporters receive status updates (if non-anonymous) within 10 business days.
- **Legal protections:** Employees are protected under the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act (Section 922), the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (Section 806), and applicable state whistleblower protection laws. External reports may be made to state insurance regulators or the SEC.

## 🔒 Security & Incident Response

> Security procedures and what to do in case of incidents.

### Phishing & Social Engineering Response

| Step | Action |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Do NOT click** any links or download attachments |
| 2 | **Do NOT reply** to the suspicious message |
| 3 | Report via the **"Report Phishing" button** in Outlook |
| 4 | Forward suspicious email to **security@rockinsurance.com** |
| 5 | If you clicked a link — **immediately** contact IT Help Desk (ext. 5000) |
| 6 | Change your password via [Password Reset Portal](#) |

### Data Breach Response Protocol

| Phase | Action | Responsible | SLA |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Detection | Identified via SIEM alerts (CrowdStrike Falcon / Splunk), endpoint detection, employee reports, or third-party notification. All anomalous events auto-escalate to the SOC. | IT Security / SOC | Real-time monitoring; triage within 15 minutes of alert |
| 2. Containment | Isolate affected systems from the network, disable compromised accounts, block malicious IPs/domains, preserve forensic evidence (disk images, memory dumps). | IT Security | Within 1 hour of confirmed incident |
| 3. Assessment | Determine scope of breach — affected systems, data types exposed (PII, PHI, financial), root cause analysis, attack vector identification. Engage third-party forensics firm if needed. | IT Security / CISO / External Forensics | Preliminary assessment within 24 hours |
| 4. Notification | Notify CISO → CEO → Board within 4 hours. Notify affected regulators (state Attorney General, DOI) within timeframes required by law (typically 30–72 hours). Notify affected individuals with remediation steps. | Legal / Compliance | Internal: 4 hours; Regulatory: per statute; Individuals: within 60 days |
| 5. Remediation | Patch vulnerabilities, rotate credentials, re-image compromised systems, update firewall rules, deploy additional monitoring. Conduct enhanced access review across all privileged accounts. | IT Security / Infrastructure | Begin within 24 hours; complete critical fixes within 72 hours |
| 6. Post-Incident Review | Conduct blameless post-mortem within 10 business days. Document lessons learned, update incident response playbooks, revise security policies, and brief executive leadership. | CISO / IT Security / Compliance | Post-mortem within 10 business days; policy updates within 30 days |

### Physical Security Procedures

| Topic | Details |
|---|---|
| Building Access | All employees must badge in at building entrances using HID proximity cards. Standard access hours are 6:00 AM – 8:00 PM Mon–Fri. After-hours access requires manager pre-approval submitted via the Facilities portal at least 24 hours in advance. Weekend access requires VP-level approval. |
| Visitor Policy | All visitors must sign in at the front desk, present government-issued photo ID, and receive a dated visitor badge. Visitors must be escorted by their host at all times in secured areas. Visitor badges must be returned upon departure. Unescorted visitors will be stopped by security. |
| Tailgating Prevention | Employees must badge in individually — do not hold doors for others, even recognized colleagues. Security cameras monitor all entry points. Report tailgating incidents to security@rockinsurance.com. Monthly tailgating awareness reminders are sent via email. |
| Lost / Stolen Badge | Report immediately to Security: security@rockinsurance.com / ext. 5500 |
| Workplace Violence | Rock Insurance maintains a zero-tolerance policy for threats, intimidation, and violence in the workplace. Any incidents or concerns should be reported immediately to HR (ext. 4000), Security (ext. 5500), or anonymously via the Compliance Hotline. Threats of immediate harm: call 911 first, then notify Security. |
| Emergency Exits | **Columbus HQ:** Exits on each floor — east and west stairwells, main lobby (Floor 1). **Phoenix:** North and south exits on each floor. **Dallas:** East and west exits on each floor. Floor wardens conduct headcounts at designated rally points. Evacuation maps are posted at all elevator banks and breakrooms. |

### Incident Severity Levels

| Level | Description | Examples | Response Time | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEV-1 (Critical) | Active, confirmed security incident with widespread impact on production systems, customer data exposure, or regulatory implications. Business operations materially affected. | Active ransomware attack, confirmed large-scale data breach (>10K records), core policy/claims system compromise, DDoS taking down customer-facing apps | Immediate — all hands on deck, 24/7 response until resolved | IT Security → CISO → CTO → CEO → Board |
| SEV-2 (High) | Confirmed or highly likely security incident with potential for significant impact. Limited data exposure or system compromise identified but not yet widespread. | Suspected data breach under investigation, compromised privileged account, malware on server, unauthorized access to production database | Within 1 hour; dedicated incident commander assigned | IT Security → CISO → CTO |
| SEV-3 (Medium) | Security event requiring investigation. No confirmed data loss or system compromise, but indicators of potential threat activity. | Targeted phishing campaign against employees, malware detected and quarantined on single endpoint, unauthorized software installation, failed brute-force attempts | Within 4 business hours | IT Security → Security Manager |
| SEV-4 (Low) | Minor security event or policy violation with minimal risk. Routine investigation required. | Single suspicious email reported (non-targeted), minor policy violation (e.g., unlocked workstation), lost USB drive (no sensitive data), accidental email to wrong recipient | Within 1 business day | IT Help Desk → IT Security (if escalation needed) |

### Reporting Channels

| Channel | Contact | When to Use |
|---|---|---|
| IT Help Desk | helpdesk@rockinsurance.com / ext. 5000 | General IT/security issues |
| Security Team | security@rockinsurance.com / ext. 5500 | Physical security, badge issues |
| Compliance Hotline | compliance@rockinsurance.com | Anonymous reporting, fraud, ethics violations |
| 911 | Emergency line | Immediate physical danger |
| Incident Report Form | [.pdf](#) | Formal documentation of any incident |

> 🚨 **If in doubt, report it.** It is always better to report a potential security concern and have it investigated than to ignore it.
